overview.text: The Broad-banded Copperhead is a venomous pit viper of the south-central United States. It used to be counted as a subspecies of the Eastern Copperhead.

identification.text: Light tan with wide dark brown crossbands (the 'broad bands'); the colour varies from red-brown to grey-brown.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Kansas, Oklahoma and central Texas, and the edges of Chihuahua and Coahuila in Mexico.

habitat.text: Light woodland with plenty of ground debris, near permanent water; it avoids crowded areas.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young. Females can sometimes reproduce without a male.

recognise.text: Wide dark crossbands on a tan body.
